findings.issue_text: [BUG] The 'tells the topic retriever to work' spec expects TopicRetriever to be invoked by the controller, but the controller enqueues Jobs::RetrieveTopic and never instantiates TopicRetriever, so this spec fails with an un-satisfied expectation. `TopicRetriever.expects(:new)` and `retriever.expects(:retrieve)` are never satisfied by `EmbedController#best` (which calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)`), so the suite fails and the after-block's `response.should be_success` assertion is never reached in a meaningful way.

[BUG] The `<%- end if %>` construct makes the entire if/else a conditional expression, so when `@topic_view.posts` is blank the else branch is never evaluated and the 'start_discussion' link is dead code. Newly created/empty topics render the embed page with neither the 'Discussion Highlights' header link nor the 'Begin the Discussion' button; users on the embedding site get a header with only the logo and no call to action.

[BUG] poll_feed calls `i.content.scrub` unconditionally, but SimpleRSS items from feeds that expose `description` instead of `content` (common RSS 2.0) have `i.content` as nil, raising NoMethodError and aborting the whole poll run. A single feed item without a content element crashes the scheduled job after the first such item; no topics are imported for that feed and every subsequent hourly poll dies at the same item (retry disabled via sidekiq_options), permanently stalling feed imports.

[BUG] The spec requires 'jobs/regular/process_post' as a dependency, which is the wrong file for Jobs::PollFeed and leaves the class unloaded unless Rails autoloading happens to resolve it via the constant reference in `describe`. The require line documents a false dependency; the spec only works because the `describe Jobs::PollFeed` constant lookup triggers autoload, and anyone copying this pattern for a standalone runner gets a NameError.

[ADVISORY] The job requires 'email/sender', a dependency with no relationship to topic retrieval; the actual dependency used is 'topic_retriever' on line 3. Copy-pasted require misleads future readers about the job's real dependencies and adds an unnecessary load; the next person extending this job builds on a wrong mental model of its requirements.

[ADVISORY] `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'` references a standalone stylesheet that is not added to the application's precompile list anywhere in this diff, so in production asset compilation the embed layout renders with a 404'd stylesheet. Embedded comment iframes on production instances load unstyled (or fail to fetch embed.css) because only application-level assets are precompiled by default; operators cannot fix it without a code change adding :embed to config.assets.precompile.

[ADVISORY] The `feed_key` method computes a Redis key from the feed polling URL but has no callers in this diff — dead code presenting itself as a caching mechanism that does not exist. The next maintainer reading poll_feed assumes feed modification state is tracked (e.g. to skip unchanged feeds) and either builds on a nonexistent mechanism or wastes time confirming it is unused; the method should be deleted until the consumer exists.

[BUG] Line 4 ends the header conditional with `<%- end if %>`, which ERB compiles to the Ruby fragment `end if` — a modifier-if with no condition — so the template raises a SyntaxError and every successful /embed/best request returns a 500. The entire embed feature 500s on its only success path; the controller specs stub TopicView and never render the template, so this is invisible to the diff's test suite.

[BUG] cook_method raw_html returns `raw` uncooked and unsanitized, and TopicEmbed.import feeds it content straight from the polled RSS feed (poll_feed.rb passes `i.content` with no HTML sanitization), producing stored XSS in both the embed iframe view (raw post.cooked) and the main Discourse topic. Whoever controls the feed_polling_url (or the embedded blog) injects arbitrary <script> into Discourse posts and the embeddable host's pages; a visitor of any embed page executes attacker script in the embeddable site's origin.

[BUG] poll_feed calls `i.content.scrub` unconditionally, but RSS 2.0 feeds expose the body as `description`, not `content` — SimpleRSS returns nil for missing elements, so `nil.scrub` raises NoMethodError and aborts the entire feed poll. Any admin who points feed_polling_url at a plain RSS 2.0 feed (the most common format) gets zero imports; the job dies with retry: false and, because TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve calls Jobs::PollFeed synchronously, embed retrieval for that URL dies too, leaving embed visitors on the loading page forever.

[BUG] The success path constructs `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)` with a topic_id fetched from topic_embeds, but never verifies the topic still exists — a topic deleted (or removed via thetrash/undelete lifecycle) after its TopicEmbed row remains returns a TopicView whose internal topic lookup raises, producing a 500 in the iframe. Every page on the embedding site that carries the embed script for a deleted topic shows a Discourse error frame instead of comments; there is no cleanup of topic_embeds rows on topic deletion anywhere in the diff.

[ADVISORY] The postMessage origin check `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring containment test, so any origin whose string is a substring of the Discourse base URL (e.g. an origin like `http://e` from a crafted page is invalid, but multi-level cases like an http URL when discourseUrl contains that substring) passes and lets the page drive iframe height — and there is no negative test for malicious origins in the diff. A malicious page embedding this script with a spoofed discourseUrl can set the iframe to arbitrary heights or, combined with any future message types, act on untrusted messages; the sibling concern is that no test covers the resize handler at all, so regressions here ship silently.

[ADVISORY] `feed_key` is defined (a 'feed-modified:' SHA1 cache key) but never referenced anywhere in the diff — the conditional-GET / If-Modified-Since handling it implies is absent, so the feed is fully re-fetched and every item re-processed every hour. Dead code signals a dropped requirement (skip unchanged feeds); maintainers pay for it as confusion, and every hourly run re-parses and re-hashes full feed contents even when nothing changed.

[ADVISORY] The RetrieveTopic job — including its embed_url presence guard, staff no_throttle branch, and user lookup — has no spec anywhere in the diff (the only job spec is spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb, which covers PollFeed only), so the enqueue contract (controller passes user_id that may be nil for anonymous visitors) is unverified. A regression in arg handling (e.g. dropping embed_url, or the nil-user anonymous path that most blog visitors take) ships untested; note the embed controller spec stubs TopicRetriever entirely, so even the nil-user_id enqueue is never exercised end-to-end.

[ADVISORY] Import appends the 'Imported from' footer via `contents << ...`, mutating the caller's string in place, and when the PostCreator result is a post that failed validations despite skip_validations (e.g. blank title from an RSS item with no <title>), TopicEmbed.create! still records topic_id/post_id from a possibly-nil post, raising or leaving orphaned embed rows that then permanently 500 the embed/best lookup via TopicView. A single malformed feed item (missing title) wedges that URL's embed permanently — every subsequent request hits the broken TopicEmbed row rather than retrying retrieval, and there is no spec covering blank-title or failed-creator import.

[BUG] An already-committed migration (CreateTopTopics) is edited in this diff to add `force: true`, which is unrelated to embed URL handling and destroys data. On any database where this migration has not yet run but top_topics exists (or is re-run via db:migrate:redo/restore), `create_table :top_topics, force: true` silently drops the existing top_topics table and all its rows; the change is also invisible to environments that already applied the migration, creating drift between schemas.

[ADVISORY] This diff modifies a previously-committed migration file with whitespace-only changes (trailing-whitespace removal, newline at EOF), scope drift with no functional purpose. Anyone reviewing or bisecting this PR sees a touched migration with no content change; it pollutes blame and suggests a rebase accident rather than intentional work traceable to the embed requirements.

[BUG] The Disqus import task's `-c/--category` option is deleted and every import is rewritten to go through TopicEmbed.import_remote, silently dropping the ability to categorize imported threads — an unrequested public-surface change to an existing rake/thor command. Any operator with existing `disqus.thor import -c "News"` scripts (or documentation referencing it) gets a Thor error for an unknown option after this deploy; all imported topics also now land uncategorized with raw-HTML cooked posts that bypass the normal cooking pipeline, where they previously got a properly cooked markdown permalink post.

[ADVISORY] The blank-line removal and `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])` change to the shared PostRevisor is only exercised by TopicEmbed.import but now applies to every caller of revise! that passes skip_validations. Any future or plugin caller that passes skip_validations now persists posts bypassing all model validations (title length, raw length, post count) with no guard that the caller is a trusted system actor; the diff introduces a global bypass mechanism for one internal use case.

[ADVISORY] The `feed_key` method (Redis "feed-modified" key built from the polling URL) is defined and never called anywhere in the diff — dead code. Maintainers reading PollFeed infer a caching/conditional-fetch mechanism that does not exist; deletion test: removing the method changes nothing, so it should be removed or wired up.

[ADVISORY] perform_retrieve synchronously executes the entire hourly-scheduled PollFeed job (Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})) inline inside a background job triggered by a single visitor's embed request, work not traceable to any requirement in the PR description. A single new embed hit causes a full RSS fetch and import of every feed item (each potentially doing open(url) + readability parsing), so one visitor's page load can spawn minutes of network work; when the feed is large this blocks the retrieve_topic worker and delays the embedding user's content past the 30s loading-page reload window.

[ADVISORY] The `embed.permalink` locale key is added but no view, controller, or job in this diff references it — a ships-inert string. Translators maintain a key with zero call sites; deletion test: removing it breaks nothing. It signals an unshipped feature (permalink links in embeds) smuggled into the locale file.

[ADVISORY] embed.js depends on two undefined globals (`discourseUrl`, `discourseEmbedUrl`) with no documentation, sample snippet, or generator anywhere in the diff telling embedders how to define them. An operator who copies embed.js from the codebase gets an iframe whose src is `undefinedembed/best?embed_url=undefined` (ReferenceError actually — the script throws and renders nothing), because the required setup variables are never shipped or described in this PR.

[BUG] perform_retrieve synchronously re-polls the entire RSS feed via Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) inside the per-pageview retrieve job, re-downloading and re-importing every feed item for each embed request. Every embed/best pageview for a not-yet-retrieved URL triggers a full feed fetch (open() over the network with no timeout) and TopicEmbed.import for every item in the feed, inside one job — an N-embeds × M-feed-items fan-out that blocks the Sidekiq worker and hammers the publisher's feed URL; if the feed URL is slow or down, all embed retrieval jobs pile up on it (cascading failure, no degradation).

[BUG] TopicEmbed.import has a check-then-insert TOCTOU race: two concurrent jobs both find no embed, both create a topic+post, then the second TopicEmbed.create! raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique. The losing transaction rolls back its TopicEmbed but the transaction wrapping PostCreator means a 500 in the retrieve job and a wasted topic creation race window; concurrent first embeds (e.g. iframe reload + feed poll) leave the loading iframe in its 30-second reload loop until one retry happens to win.

[BUG] In the update branch post = embed.post is used with no nil guard, so a deleted/trashed post (embed row persists) crashes PostRevisor.new(nil). Once the referenced post is deleted but the topic_embeds row survives, every subsequent feed poll for that item raises NoMethodError, and since PollFeed's items loop has no per-item error handling, one broken item aborts processing of the entire feed — all later items stop importing.

[BUG] i.content is called with no nil check, so any feed item lacking a <content> element (summary/description-only feeds are common) crashes the whole poll. A single item without content raises NoMethodError on nil, aborting the items loop mid-feed, so all subsequent feed items — including new articles — are silently never imported; the hourly schedule retries the same failure every hour with no error surfacing (retry: false).

[ADVISORY] The embeddable_host setting is compared raw against URI(referer).host and URI(embed_url).host with no normalization on either side, so an admin entering a value with a scheme, port, or trailing slash (e.g. 'http://eviltrout.com') makes the equality check fail for every request. The whole embed feature silently 403s (or never retrieves) with no diagnostic telling the admin the setting must be a bare host; the same drift also applies to 'www.' prefixes between referer host and feed item links, permanently breaking retrieval for those URLs.

[ADVISORY] The new posts.cook_method column default of 1 is a magic integer discriminator with no named DB constraint, and Post.cook_methods is the only translation — any consumer reading posts.cook_method directly (analytics, plugins, future code) sees bare 1/2. A future cook method added to the Ruby Enum with no corresponding awareness in downstream consumers silently misroutes; the enum is also ordered so :regular=1 but the column default is hardcoded as the literal 1, so reordering the Enum silently changes what existing rows mean.

[ADVISORY] The raw_html cook path returns before Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...), so all after_post_cook plugin filters and post_analyzer are silently skipped for imported posts. Any site running plugins that rely on after_post_cook (emoji, onebox post-processing, custom filters) gets posts where the filter never runs; the plugin API contract 'after_post_cook runs for every cooked post' is broken by this new branch with no way for a plugin to opt back in.

[ADVISORY] feed_key is defined (a sha1-keyed cache key for the feed's modified state) but never used anywhere — the conditional-fetch caching it implies was never wired up. Dead code implying If-Modified-Since/etag-based polling exists; the actual implementation re-downloads the full feed every hour and on every retrieve job, so the next maintainer trusts a cache that isn't there.

[ADVISORY] The loading view unconditionally reloads every 30 seconds with no retry cap or failure signal, so a URL that can never be retrieved (non-HTML page, readability returns no content, host mismatch between referer and embed_url) loops forever. Every visitor's browser on a permanently-failing embed page hammers /embed/best every 30 seconds indefinitely, each hit re-enqueueing retrieve_topic jobs (throttled only to 1/min per URL), producing unbounded traffic and job churn with no terminal state.

[ADVISORY] force: true was added to an unrelated existing migration's create_table, so re-running migrations (or the fresh-vs-existing path) silently drops any existing top_topics table and its data. Any environment where top_topics already exists loses all its rows when this migration runs — derived/aggregated ranking data destroyed with no backfill, purely to accommodate a developer's local re-run.

[ADVISORY] absolutize_urls only rewrites href/src beginning with a single '/', leaving protocol-relative URLs ('//cdn.example.com/img.png') and bare relative paths ('images/wat.jpg') untouched. Imported articles from feeds that use protocol-relative or bare-relative asset URLs render broken images/links in both the Discourse topic and the embed iframe, and since content_sha1 won't change, they stay broken through every re-poll.

[ADVISORY] topic_embeds has no index on topic_id or post_id and no FK constraints, though topic_id_for_embed and the belongs_to traversals query/iterate by those columns. Deleting a topic or post leaves an orphaned embed row whose embed_url still resolves to a dead topic_id — /embed/best then constructs TopicView on a deleted topic and 500s — and there is no index backing any future lookup by topic_id.

[BUG] PollFeed stores raw RSS item content directly into posts via TopicEmbed.import with cook_method raw_html, with no HTML sanitization, unlike the import_remote path which filters tags through Readability. A malicious or compromised RSS feed injects arbitrary <script> markup that is stored verbatim (Post#cook returns raw for raw_html) and rendered to embed viewers via `raw post.cooked` in best.html.erb — stored XSS on the Discourse host executing in the context of the embed iframe parent page contract.

[BUG] The postMessage origin check uses substring containment (`discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`) instead of an exact origin match. Any attacker page whose origin string appears anywhere within the discourseUrl value (e.g. a page served from `https://discourse.example.evil.com/` when discourseUrl is `https://discourse.example.evil.com` style substrings, or any origin that is a substring of the URL including path/query) passes the check and can drive the iframe height (and any future message types) on every site embedding Discourse comments.

[BUG] The diff adds `force: true` to the existing create_top_topics migration, so running pending migrations on an already-deployed instance drops the existing top_topics table and recreates it empty. Operators deploying this change lose all top_topics aggregate data (daily/weekly/monthly counters) on every existing forum, silently and irrecoverably, just to make the migration re-runnable in dev.

[BUG] The raw_html cook path returns `raw` before Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...) is invoked, so plugins registered on the after_post_cook hook are silently skipped for raw_html posts. Any site with a plugin relying on after_post_cook (e.g. for link rewriting, oneboxing, or content filtering) sees imported/embedded topics bypass the filter entirely — the public plugin contract changes with no documentation or opt-out.

[ADVISORY] The disqus import task silently changes objective: it drops the `--category` option and replaces the local permalink-post creation with a remote fetch via TopicEmbed.import_remote, altering what the command produces. Existing operator scripts passing `-c <category>` now fail with an unknown-option error, and imported threads no longer contain the `[Permalink](...)` body — instead the article is scraped from the live site at import time, which fails or produces different content if the source is unreachable. This behavioral change shipped without any migration note or explicit acceptance.

[ADVISORY] feed_key (a SHA1-keyed 'feed-modified' cache key) is defined but never called anywhere in the diff, so the PollFeed job re-imports every feed item every hour with no conditional-get or modification check. The only per-item guard is the content_sha1 comparison in TopicEmbed.import; titles-only changes or per-item churn cause a full RSS parse and N PostRevisor revisions every hour for every feed item, and the dead method suggests a dropped requirement (conditional fetching) that was silently descoped.

[ADVISORY] The loading view reloads the iframe every 30 seconds unconditionally, with no failure terminal state. When retrieve_topic fails permanently (invalid embeddable_host mismatch discovered only inside the job, feed fetch error, or embed_by_username user deleted), embed visitors get an infinite reload loop that hammers the embed endpoint every 30s per viewer instead of any error message.

[ADVISORY] The referer host check compares `URI(request.referer).host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host` as a case-sensitive exact string. Browsers send referer hosts in lowercase per spec but SiteSetting values are admin-entered free text: an admin who enters 'Eviltrout.com' locks out every embed, and 'evilTrout.com' vs 'eviltrout.com' mismatches yield confusing 403s with no admin feedback.

[BUG] The new raw_html cook method returns unsanitized `raw` content verbatim, and that content is attacker-controllable feed/article HTML, so any script/event-handler markup in an RSS item or scraped article becomes stored XSS rendered to every visitor of the embed iframe. An attacker who controls or compromises the polled feed (feed_polling_url) injects `

[BUG] TopicEmbed.import string-interpolates the embed `url` into an HTML attribute and body (`"#{url}"`) that is stored as raw_html, so a URL containing a single quote and event handler breaks out of the attribute and executes script. A feed item (or scraped article) whose link is `http://eviltrout.com/x' onmouseover='alert(1)` — which passes both the `^https?://` check on line 11 and TopicRetriever's host-only comparison — injects arbitrary HTML/JS attributes into the post rendered via `raw post.cooked` on the public embed page, giving stored XSS on the Discourse origin.

[BUG] The layout interpolates `request.referer` unescaped into a JavaScript string literal (`'<%= request.referer %>'`), so a Referer header containing a single quote and script breaks out of the string and executes arbitrary JS in the rendered page. Any client that sends a crafted Referer (headers are fully client-controlled; the referer-host check in EmbedController#ensure_embeddable is a separate request-time check but the value still flows here unescaped — and non-browser clients bypass it entirely) gets JS injection into the /embed/best response, e.g. `Referer: http://x');alert(1);//` executes on load; combined with the ALLOWALL X-Frame-Options this reaches embedded-page visitors.

[ADVISORY] The only gate on /embed/best is a Referer header check (`URI(request.referer).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`), which is client-supplied and trivially forged by any non-browser client, so the route's throttled content-retrieval and topic rendering are effectively unauthenticated. Anyone can curl /embed/best with a forged Referer to enumerate/refresh TopicEmbed content and to drive RetrieveTopic jobs; the 60s Redis throttle in TopicRetriever is per-URL and skipped for staff, so a scripted loop over URLs still triggers a server-side fetch of embeddable_host URLs (a content-scraping amplification surface), and the topic content served is whatever the embedding configured — referer-based auth is a trust-the-client design that OWASP classifies as insecure design.

[ADVISORY] The postMessage origin check uses substring containment (`discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`) instead of strict equality, so any origin whose string contains the Discourse URL passes. A malicious origin such as `http://evil.com/?http://forum.example.com` or a subdomain-suffix trick containing the full discourse URL substring sends `discourse-resize` messages that the embedding page accepts; because the handler only sets iframe height the direct impact is limited (no sensitive data read), but the weak origin gate is a latent XSS/data-theft primitive if the handler ever grows to trust message payloads — and the correct fix (===, or parsed-origin comparison) is one line.

[BUG] The 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' tests verify nothing about those guards: feed_polling_enabled? is not stubbed in them, so the real SiteSetting default (feed_polling_enabled: false in config/site_settings.yml) short-circuits execute and poll_feed is never called regardless of the setting under test. Deleting the `SiteSetting.feed_polling_url.present?` or `SiteSetting.embed_by_username.present?` conditions from Jobs::PollFeed#execute would still pass this suite, so a regression that polls a nil feed URL (crashing `open(nil)` in poll_feed) ships green.

[BUG] The 'is 404 without an embed_url' test attributes the failure to the missing embed_url, but the before_filter ensure_embeddable runs before params.require and raises Discourse::InvalidAccess first because SiteSetting.embeddable_host is '' (unstubbed in this test), so params.require(:embed_url) is never reached. Removing the `params.require(:embed_url)` guard from EmbedController#best would not fail this test; the test's assertion (`response.should_not be_success`) is satisfied by the host-check rejection it actually exercises, giving false confidence that the param contract is covered.

[BUG] The 'creates a topic view' test replaces the unit under test with a mock: TopicView.expects(:new) returns nil, so @topic_view is nil, and since the spec never calls render_views, the best.html.erb template (which dereferences @topic_view.posts and @topic_view.topic.url) is never rendered — the test asserts the mock was constructed and nothing else. A regression that assigns @topic_view = nil, passes wrong options, or breaks the view template entirely still passes this test; the only success-path assertion lives in the shared `after` block which never touches rendered content or assigns.

[BUG] Every test in the 'with a valid host' context stubs retrieved_recently?, so the real throttle implementation in TopicRetriever (the $redis setnx/expire 60-second logic, including the no_throttle: true branch used by Jobs::RetrieveTopic for staff) is never executed by any test in the diff. A regression in retrieved_recently? — e.g. the setnx key never expiring, permanently blocking all embed retrievals, or the no_throttle flag being ignored so staff are throttled too — passes this suite untouched, and the production symptom is embedded comment threads that never populate.

[ADVISORY] All five tests stub or expect perform_retrieve, so the entire retrieval pipeline the spec file nominally guards — perform_retrieve's existing-embed bail, the PollFeed trigger, and fetch_http's user lookup / import_remote call — has zero executed coverage in this diff. The path that Jobs::RetrieveTopic actually invokes in production (TopicRetriever#retrieve → perform_retrieve → fetch_http) can regress arbitrarily — e.g. fetch_http crashing on a missing embed_by_username user being nil and .downcase raising NoMethodError — without any test failing.

[ADVISORY] The 'Supports updating the post' test asserts only `post.cooked =~ /new contents/`, which is trivially true under raw_html cooking (cooked == raw), so it never verifies the revision machinery the update path exercises — PostRevisor#revise! with skip_validations/bypass_rate_limiter, or that embed.content_sha1 is updated to prevent re-revision. A regression where TopicEmbed#import skips the revisor entirely (returning the stale post) or never updates content_sha1 (re-revising every post on every hourly poll) still passes this test; RSS-driven sites silently churn revisions or never pick up edits.

[ADVISORY] The new cook short-circuit `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` skips Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...) entirely — a behavior change in the core cooking pipeline with no test anywhere in the diff that registers or asserts an after_post_cook filter against a raw_html post. A plugin relying on after_post_cook (e.g. to sanitize injected HTML on every cooked post) is silently dropped for RSS-imported posts, and since topic_embed_spec only asserts `post.cooked == post.raw`, the filter-skipping behavior is an untested divergence from the documented cook contract.

[ADVISORY] The success assertions (`response.should be_success`, X-Frame-Options header) live in an `after` block rather than per-example `it` assertions, so any example added inside the 'success' context that merely exercises a broken branch still 'passes' via the after block's evaluation of the last successful request state, and a failing header check is reported against whichever example ran last. Future test authors adding cases to this context get misleading failure attribution and an implicit success contract that reads as a side effect rather than an assertion, degrading change-safety of the controller spec.

[BUG] An already-shipped migration (CreateTopTopics, dated 20131223, i.e. present on existing production databases) was retroactively edited to add `force: true` to its create_table, making the migration destructive on re-run. On any environment that already ran this migration and then re-runs it (db:migrate:redo, a rollback/down followed by up, or restoring schema_migrations state after a partial deploy), `create_table :top_topics, force: true` silently DROPs the existing top_topics table and all its rows — computed top-topic metrics data is irreversibly destroyed with no backup step, and the drop happens inside a migration whose down cannot restore the data.

[ADVISORY] The new TopicEmbeds migration uses `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`, building destructive behavior into the migration itself. If this table ever exists when the migration runs again (a re-run after a failed deploy where the transaction committed, a restore, or an operator re-running pending migrations against a partially-migrated DB), all topic_embeds rows are silently dropped; TopicEmbed.import then re-creates duplicate topics for every embedded URL because the embed_url uniqueness record is gone. A plain create_table would fail loudly instead.

[ADVISORY] `embed_url` is a 255-char varchar with a unique index, but embed URLs from real-world pages (long query strings, tracking params) routinely exceed 255 characters and there is no truncation or length validation upstream. TopicEmbed.import on a >255-char feed item link raises a value-too-long error (MySQL strict / PG) inside the PollFeed job with `retry: false`, aborting processing of all remaining feed items in that run; on MySQL non-strict it silently truncates, which then collides on the unique index with a different URL sharing the truncated prefix, failing the import with a duplicate-key error on a URL that was never embedded.

[ADVISORY] topic_id and post_id are plain integer columns with null: false but no foreign-key constraints and no composite uniqueness, while TopicEmbed rows are the sole record mapping an embed_url to its topic. If a referenced topic or post is later deleted (e.g., by a moderator purge or a deletion routine that doesn't know about topic_embeds), the topic_embeds row survives as an orphan; TopicEmbed.import then takes the update path, calls PostRevisor.new(nil-post).revise! and raises NoMethodError, permanently breaking re-import and the embed/best view for that URL until the stale row is manually cleaned up — there is no cleanup path in this diff.

[BUG] content_sha1 is committed via update_column without checking the result of PostRevisor#revise!, so a failed revision permanently marks the content as imported. If revise! fails (returns false, or @post.save with validate: false still fails at the DB level), embed.content_sha1 is updated anyway, so every subsequent poll/feed import sees the hash as unchanged and never retries the update — the topic silently diverges from the source article forever with no error logged.

[BUG] import_remote calls open(url) with no timeout and reads the entire body into memory with no size cap. A slow or hung embeddable host blocks the Sidekiq RetrieveTopic worker (and the scheduled PollFeed path that reaches here) indefinitely on a stalled TCP connection, and a huge page OOMs the worker process; this runs on the request-triggered /embed/best path, so one bad target URL wedges the job queue's workers.

[BUG] poll_feed calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) with no timeout, and the job is configured sidekiq_options retry: false. A hung feed server blocks the scheduled job worker indefinitely, and any exception (network error, malformed feed, nil i.content causing NoMethodError on scrub) fails the job with retries disabled — feed importing silently stops for all subsequent hours until someone notices, with no surfaced error to any operator.

[BUG] The retrieved_recently? throttle key is committed via $redis.setnx before perform_retrieve runs, so a failed or retried retrieval no-ops 'successfully'. When perform_retrieve raises (open-uri error, Readability parse failure), Sidekiq's default retry re-runs RetrieveTopic, but the 60-second throttle key makes the retried job silently skip the retrieval and report success — the TopicEmbed is never created and the client-side loading page reload loop never converges on content.

[BUG] The loading page unconditionally reloads every 30 seconds with no failure path and no retry cap. An end user on the embedding site whose retrieve job failed (invalid content, fetch error, throttle collision) gets an infinite reload loop of the 'Loading Discussion...' page for as long as they leave the page open — the failure is invisible to them and to the site operator, with no error state ever rendered.

[ADVISORY] feed_key (the modified-hash Redis key) is computed but never read or written, so the intended poll-throttle/dedup mechanism is inert.
