adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `embed.permalink` in `config/locales/server.en.yml`, and none of the newly added embed views (`app/views/embed/best.html.erb`, `loading.html.erb`, `layouts/embed.html.erb`) or related controller/job code references that key (they use `embed.title`, `embed.start_discussion`, `embed.continue`, `embed.loading`, `embed.imported_from`). However, an unused locale string is not a verifiable defect or a substantial review issue in this PR; it’s a minor cleanliness/nit concern rather than something that breaks behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] embed.js depends on two undefined globals (`discourseUrl`, `discourseEmbedUrl`) with no documentation, sample snippet, or generator anywhere in the diff telling embedders how to define them. An operator who copies embed.js from the codebase gets an iframe whose src is `undefinedembed/best?embed_url=undefined` (ReferenceError actually — the script throws and renders nothing), because the required setup variables are never shipped or described in this PR.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js` the script directly references two globals (`discourseUrl` and `discourseEmbedUrl`) and only annotates them via comments (`/* global ... */`). The diff does not add any initializer snippet, generator, or documentation showing embedders how these variables are defined, nor is `embed.js` included from any layout in the diff (the new `embed.html.erb` only includes the stylesheet). So the finding that the embed script has an undocumented required configuration is grounded in the diff. While this isn’t an internal runtime bug if the intended integration defines those globals elsewhere, it is a concrete integration/documentation gap introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] perform_retrieve synchronously re-polls the entire RSS feed via Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) inside the per-pageview retrieve job, re-downloading and re-importing every feed item for each embed request. Every embed/best pageview for a not-yet-retrieved URL triggers a full feed fetch (open() over the network with no timeout) and TopicEmbed.import for every item in the feed, inside one job — an N-embeds × M-feed-items fan-out that blocks the Sidekiq worker and hammers the publisher's feed URL; if the feed URL is slow or down, all embed retrieval jobs pile up on it (cascading failure, no degradation).

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true it calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously (not enqueued) for every embed URL that is not yet in `topic_embeds` (`return if TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?` happens before the feed poll). `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` (network I/O, no timeout shown) and then iterates `rss.items.each` calling `TopicEmbed.import(...)` for every item. This matches the finding: a single embed retrieval can trigger a full feed fetch/import, potentially repeated per embed request/job, blocking the Sidekiq worker and hammering the feed URL.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] TopicEmbed.import has a check-then-insert TOCTOU race: two concurrent jobs both find no embed, both create a topic+post, then the second TopicEmbed.create! raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique. The losing transaction rolls back its TopicEmbed but the transaction wrapping PostCreator means a 500 in the retrieve job and a wasted topic creation race window; concurrent first embeds (e.g. iframe reload + feed poll) leave the loading iframe in its 30-second reload loop until one retry happens to win.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a classic check-then-insert race in `TopicEmbed.import`: it does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and, if blank, enters `Topic.transaction` and calls `TopicEmbed.create!` (topic_embed.rb). The migration adds `add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`, so two concurrent imports for the same URL can both observe no row and then the second `create!` will raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`. There is no rescue around this in `TopicEmbed.import` / `TopicRetriever` / `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`, so the losing job will error out. The exact user-visible impact (e.g., “stuck in reload loop”) depends on timing, but the unhandled uniqueness exception + race is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In the update branch post = embed.post is used with no nil guard, so a deleted/trashed post (embed row persists) crashes PostRevisor.new(nil). Once the referenced post is deleted but the topic_embeds row survives, every subsequent feed poll for that item raises NoMethodError, and since PollFeed's items loop has no per-item error handling, one broken item aborts processing of the entire feed — all later items stop importing.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path assumes `embed.post` exists: `post = embed.post` followed by `PostRevisor.new(post)` when content changes. If the referenced post has been deleted (no DB foreign key shown; only `post_id null: false` + unique index on `embed_url`), `embed.post` can be `nil`, leading to an exception when revising. Additionally, `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` iterates `rss.items.each` without per-item error handling, so any exception from `TopicEmbed.import` would abort processing of the remaining feed items.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] i.content is called with no nil check, so any feed item lacking a <content> element (summary/description-only feeds are common) crashes the whole poll. A single item without content raises NoMethodError on nil, aborting the items loop mid-feed, so all subsequent feed items — including new articles — are silently never imported; the hourly schedule retries the same failure every hour with no error surfacing (retry: false).

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the loop does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If a feed item lacks a `<content>` element, `i.content` can be `nil`, and calling `.scrub` on `nil` will raise `NoMethodError`, aborting the job mid-loop and preventing subsequent items from being imported.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The embeddable_host setting is compared raw against URI(referer).host and URI(embed_url).host with no normalization on either side, so an admin entering a value with a scheme, port, or trailing slash (e.g. 'http://eviltrout.com') makes the equality check fail for every request. The whole embed feature silently 403s (or never retrieves) with no diagnostic telling the admin the setting must be a bare host; the same drift also applies to 'www.' prefixes between referer host and feed item links, permanently breaking retrieval for those URLs.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces strict string equality checks between `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` and `URI(...).host` without any normalization. In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, it rejects requests when `URI(request.referer).host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, and in `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` it rejects retrieval when `URI(@embed_url).host` differs from the setting. If an admin enters `embeddable_host` with a scheme/port/trailing slash (e.g. `http://eviltrout.com`), that value will never equal a bare host like `eviltrout.com`, breaking embedding/retrieval. Similarly, `www.` vs non-`www.` host differences will cause rejection. The raised messages (`'invalid referer host'`) don’t guide the admin toward the required bare-host format.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new posts.cook_method column default of 1 is a magic integer discriminator with no named DB constraint, and Post.cook_methods is the only translation — any consumer reading posts.cook_method directly (analytics, plugins, future code) sees bare 1/2. A future cook method added to the Ruby Enum with no corresponding awareness in downstream consumers silently misroutes; the enum is also ordered so :regular=1 but the column default is hardcoded as the literal 1, so reordering the Enum silently changes what existing rows mean.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `posts.cook_method` as an `integer` with a hardcoded DB default (`add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false`) while the only semantic mapping is in Ruby (`Post.cook_methods ||= Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)`). This creates an implicit “magic number” contract in the database: any code/consumer reading the column directly will see `1/2`, and changing the enum ordering/definition later could change meaning without any DB-level constraint or explicit mapping update. That’s a maintainability/architecture risk introduced by this change, not an immediately verifiable runtime defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The raw_html cook path returns before Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...), so all after_post_cook plugin filters and post_analyzer are silently skipped for imported posts. Any site running plugins that rely on after_post_cook (emoji, onebox post-processing, custom filters) gets posts where the filter never runs; the plugin API contract 'after_post_cook runs for every cooked post' is broken by this new branch with no way for a plugin to opt back in.

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/post.rb, Post#cook now returns early for cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html] (`return raw ...`), which bypasses both `post_analyzer.cook(*args)` and `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)`. TopicEmbed.import sets `cook_method: ...[:raw_html]`, so imported posts will not run after_post_cook filters. The diff clearly introduces this behavior; whether it violates a plugin API contract is not verifiable from the diff, but the compatibility concern is real and specific.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] feed_key is defined (a sha1-keyed cache key for the feed's modified state) but never used anywhere — the conditional-fetch caching it implies was never wired up. Dead code implying If-Modified-Since/etag-based polling exists; the actual implementation re-downloads the full feed every hour and on every retrieve job, so the next maintainer trusts a cache that isn't there.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the method `feed_key` is defined (building a SHA1-based Redis key from `SiteSetting.feed_polling_url`) but is never called anywhere in the diff. The actual `poll_feed` implementation always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with no If-Modified-Since/ETag logic, and `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` may invoke `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})`, so the presence of `feed_key` does imply intended caching that is not wired up. This is dead/incomplete code and a maintainability/performance concern, but not a functional correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The loading view unconditionally reloads every 30 seconds with no retry cap or failure signal, so a URL that can never be retrieved (non-HTML page, readability returns no content, host mismatch between referer and embed_url) loops forever. Every visitor's browser on a permanently-failing embed page hammers /embed/best every 30 seconds indefinitely, each hit re-enqueueing retrieve_topic jobs (throttled only to 1/min per URL), producing unbounded traffic and job churn with no terminal state.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb` the client unconditionally reloads the page every 30 seconds (`setTimeout(... document.location.reload();, 30000);`) with no cap or error state. In `EmbedController#best`, when no embed exists it always enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `loading`. If the embed can never be created (e.g., `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` returns true because `URI(@embed_url).host` != `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, or remote fetch/parsing fails), the page will stay in the loading state forever and each reload will enqueue another `retrieve_topic` job. Although `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` throttles the actual fetch to 60s per URL, the browser traffic to `/embed/best` and job enqueuing will continue indefinitely with no terminal behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] force: true was added to an unrelated existing migration's create_table, so re-running migrations (or the fresh-vs-existing path) silently drops any existing top_topics table and its data. Any environment where top_topics already exists loses all its rows when this migration runs — derived/aggregated ranking data destroyed with no backfill, purely to accommodate a developer's local re-run.

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb the diff changes `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. In ActiveRecord, `force: true` drops an existing table before creating it, so if this migration is ever run against a DB that already has `top_topics` (e.g., a partially-initialized DB, a re-run in a nonstandard workflow), it will destroy all existing rows in that table with no backfill in the migration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] absolutize_urls only rewrites href/src beginning with a single '/', leaving protocol-relative URLs ('//cdn.example.com/img.png') and bare relative paths ('images/wat.jpg') untouched. Imported articles from feeds that use protocol-relative or bare-relative asset URLs render broken images/links in both the Discourse topic and the embed iframe, and since content_sha1 won't change, they stay broken through every re-poll.

adjudication.rationale: `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls` only rewrites `href`/`src` values when they `start_with?('/')` (see `if href.present? && href.start_with?('/')` and same for `src`). This leaves bare relative paths like `images/wat.jpg` untouched (broken when rendered outside the original page context). Additionally, protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/x.png` also match `start_with?('/')` but will be rewritten incorrectly because `sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips both slashes, producing `#{prefix}/cdn.example.com/x.png` instead of preserving the CDN host. Separately, `content_sha1` is computed from the pre-absolutized `contents`, so even if the rewriting logic changes later, unchanged feed content won't trigger an update (`if content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1`), leaving already-imported broken URLs unrevised.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] topic_embeds has no index on topic_id or post_id and no FK constraints, though topic_id_for_embed and the belongs_to traversals query/iterate by those columns. Deleting a topic or post leaves an orphaned embed row whose embed_url still resolves to a dead topic_id — /embed/best then constructs TopicView on a deleted topic and 500s — and there is no index backing any future lookup by topic_id.

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateTopicEmbeds` creates `topic_embeds` with a unique index only on `embed_url` and no indexes on `topic_id`/`post_id`, and it adds no foreign key constraints (diff: `db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb`). Given `belongs_to :topic` / `belongs_to :post` in `TopicEmbed`, orphaned rows are possible if topics/posts are deleted because there is no FK or dependent cleanup shown in the diff. However, the finding overstates current query usage: `topic_id_for_embed` looks up by `embed_url` (which *is* indexed), and `belongs_to` traversals query the parent tables by primary key, not requiring an index on `topic_id`/`post_id`. The claimed `/embed/best` 500 on deleted topics is plausible but not directly verifiable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] PollFeed stores raw RSS item content directly into posts via TopicEmbed.import with cook_method raw_html, with no HTML sanitization, unlike the import_remote path which filters tags through Readability. A malicious or compromised RSS feed injects arbitrary <script> markup that is stored verbatim (Post#cook returns raw for raw_html) and rendered to embed viewers via `raw post.cooked` in best.html.erb — stored XSS on the Discourse host executing in the context of the embed iframe parent page contract.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an RSS polling path that takes `i.content` from a remote feed (`SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`) and passes it to `TopicEmbed.import` after only `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` (no HTML sanitization). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` verbatim for `raw_html`, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. The embed view renders with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, so any `<script>`/event-handler HTML from the feed would be stored and rendered, enabling stored XSS in the Discourse embed iframe. By contrast, `import_remote` does apply Readability tag/attribute filtering, reinforcing the inconsistency noted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The postMessage origin check uses substring containment (`discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`) instead of an exact origin match. Any attacker page whose origin string appears anywhere within the discourseUrl value (e.g. a page served from `https://discourse.example.evil.com/` when discourseUrl is `https://discourse.example.evil.com` style substrings, or any origin that is a substring of the URL including path/query) passes the check and can drive the iframe height (and any future message types) on every site embedding Discourse comments.
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same security flaw: origin validation uses `indexOf`/substring containment rather than an exact origin match, allowing bypass with attacker-controlled domains that contain the expected domain as a substring (e.g., evil-discourseUrl.com / discourse.example.evil.com).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The diff adds `force: true` to the existing create_top_topics migration, so running pending migrations on an already-deployed instance drops the existing top_topics table and recreates it empty. Operators deploying this change lose all top_topics aggregate data (daily/weekly/monthly counters) on every existing forum, silently and irrecoverably, just to make the migration re-runnable in dev.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `create_table :top_topics` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true` in `20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb`, and `force: true` would drop an existing table *if that migration is executed*. However, on an already-deployed instance that has previously run this migration, Rails will not re-run it (it’s tracked in `schema_migrations` by version), so deploying this change does not “drop the existing top_topics table” for every forum via pending migrations as claimed. The finding overstates an effect that is not verifiable from the diff’s behavior under normal migration execution.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The raw_html cook path returns `raw` before Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...) is invoked, so plugins registered on the after_post_cook hook are silently skipped for raw_html posts. Any site with a plugin relying on after_post_cook (e.g. for link rewriting, oneboxing, or content filtering) sees imported/embedded topics bypass the filter entirely — the public plugin contract changes with no documentation or opt-out.

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/post.rb, Post#cook now early-returns `raw` when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, which bypasses the existing `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)` call that still runs for the regular path. This is a concrete behavior change introduced by the diff: any raw_html posts (e.g., those created in TopicEmbed.import via PostCreator with cook_method :raw_html) will not invoke the after_post_cook plugin hook at all, potentially breaking plugin behavior that relies on that hook.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The disqus import task silently changes objective: it drops the `--category` option and replaces the local permalink-post creation with a remote fetch via TopicEmbed.import_remote, altering what the command produces. Existing operator scripts passing `-c <category>` now fail with an unknown-option error, and imported threads no longer contain the `[Permalink](...)` body — instead the article is scraped from the live site at import time, which fails or produces different content if the source is unreachable. This behavioral change shipped without any migration note or explicit acceptance.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly removes the Disqus Thor task option `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` and deletes the code that mapped it to a `category_id` (lib/tasks/disqus.thor). Any existing usage passing `-c/--category` would now raise an unknown-option error (broken CLI behavior). The diff also replaces creating a local post body containing a `[Permalink](...)` with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, which fetches/scrapes remote content at import time instead of importing the thread link deterministically, changing output and introducing a new dependency on source availability.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] feed_key (a SHA1-keyed 'feed-modified' cache key) is defined but never called anywhere in the diff, so the PollFeed job re-imports every feed item every hour with no conditional-get or modification check. The only per-item guard is the content_sha1 comparison in TopicEmbed.import; titles-only changes or per-item churn cause a full RSS parse and N PostRevisor revisions every hour for every feed item, and the dead method suggests a dropped requirement (conditional fetching) that was silently descoped.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `feed_key` is defined (SHA1 "feed-modified" cache key) but never referenced. `poll_feed` always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates `rss.items.each`, calling `TopicEmbed.import` for every item on every run, with no conditional GET / last-modified/etag check in this diff. However, this is primarily an efficiency/scope concern rather than a verifiable correctness bug: `TopicEmbed.import` dedupes by `embed_url` and only revises when `content_sha1` changes, so it won’t necessarily re-import/revise every hour.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The loading view reloads the iframe every 30 seconds unconditionally, with no failure terminal state. When retrieve_topic fails permanently (invalid embeddable_host mismatch discovered only inside the job, feed fetch error, or embed_by_username user deleted), embed visitors get an infinite reload loop that hammers the embed endpoint every 30s per viewer instead of any error message.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb` the page unconditionally `document.location.reload()` every 30000ms. In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is nil it always enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders `loading`. If the job can never create a `TopicEmbed` record (e.g., `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` returns true because `embed_url` host != `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, or `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` returns early when `embed_by_username` user is missing), the embed will stay on the loading page and reload forever, repeatedly hitting `GET /embed/best` and repeatedly enqueueing the job.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The referer host check compares `URI(request.referer).host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host` as a case-sensitive exact string. Browsers send referer hosts in lowercase per spec but SiteSetting values are admin-entered free text: an admin who enters 'Eviltrout.com' locks out every embed, and 'evilTrout.com' vs 'eviltrout.com' mismatches yield confusing 403s with no admin feedback.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, the referer host is checked via an exact, case-sensitive string comparison: `URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. There is no normalization (e.g., downcasing) of `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, which is free-text admin input (see `config/site_settings.yml`). Since DNS hostnames are case-insensitive, entering `Eviltrout.com` would incorrectly fail against a lowercase referer host and raise `Discourse::InvalidAccess`, effectively breaking embedding. The same exact-string host comparison also appears in `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new raw_html cook method returns unsanitized `raw` content verbatim, and that content is attacker-controllable feed/article HTML, so any script/event-handler markup in an RSS item or scraped article becomes stored XSS rendered to every visitor of the embed iframe. An attacker who controls or compromises the polled feed (feed_polling_url) injects `

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a `:raw_html` cook method that makes `Post#cook` return `raw` verbatim (`app/models/post.rb`), bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and uses feed/article HTML as `raw` (after only URL absolutization), and the feed polling path (`app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`) passes `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` directly into `TopicEmbed.import` with no sanitization. The embed view then renders HTML with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (`app/views/embed/best.html.erb`), so attacker-controlled markup from a compromised/malicious feed/article can execute as script/event-handler HTML in the Discourse origin inside the iframe (stored XSS). The readability path has a tag/attribute allowlist but does not show any scheme filtering for `href`/`src`, so `javascript:` URLs are also plausible.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] TopicEmbed.import string-interpolates the embed `url` into an HTML attribute and body (`"#{url}"`) that is stored as raw_html, so a URL containing a single quote and event handler breaks out of the attribute and executes script. A feed item (or scraped article) whose link is `http://eviltrout.com/x' onmouseover='alert(1)` — which passes both the `^https?://` check on line 11 and TopicRetriever's host-only comparison — injects arbitrary HTML/JS attributes into the post rendered via `raw post.cooked` on the public embed page, giving stored XSS on the Discourse origin.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the `url` is interpolated directly into HTML (`"#{url}"`) and appended to `contents`, then stored via `PostCreator` with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (so `Post#cook` returns `raw` unchanged). The embed view renders this with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, so any quotes in `url` can break out of the single-quoted `href` attribute and inject arbitrary attributes/HTML. The only URL check is `/^https?:\/\//`, which does not prevent quotes, and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` compares only `URI(@embed_url).host`, so a crafted URL with a valid host but containing `'` in the path can reach this code path. This is a stored XSS on the Discourse origin.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The layout interpolates `request.referer` unescaped into a JavaScript string literal (`'<%= request.referer %>'`), so a Referer header containing a single quote and script breaks out of the string and executes arbitrary JS in the rendered page. Any client that sends a crafted Referer (headers are fully client-controlled; the referer-host check in EmbedController#ensure_embeddable is a separate request-time check but the value still flows here unescaped — and non-browser clients bypass it entirely) gets JS injection into the /embed/best response, e.g. `Referer: http://x');alert(1);//` executes on load; combined with the ALLOWALL X-Frame-Options this reaches embedded-page visitors.
matched_golden_ids: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue describes `request.referer` being interpolated into a JavaScript string literal without escaping, enabling an attacker-controlled Referer header to break out of the string and execute arbitrary JavaScript (XSS). This is the same underlying vulnerability described in the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The only gate on /embed/best is a Referer header check (`URI(request.referer).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`), which is client-supplied and trivially forged by any non-browser client, so the route's throttled content-retrieval and topic rendering are effectively unauthenticated. Anyone can curl /embed/best with a forged Referer to enumerate/refresh TopicEmbed content and to drive RetrieveTopic jobs; the 60s Redis throttle in TopicRetriever is per-URL and skipped for staff, so a scripted loop over URLs still triggers a server-side fetch of embeddable_host URLs (a content-scraping amplification surface), and the topic content served is whatever the embedding configured — referer-based auth is a trust-the-client design that OWASP classifies as insecure design.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, the only access control is `URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host` (plus `embeddable_host` presence). This is entirely based on the client-supplied Referer header and can be trivially spoofed by non-browser clients. With a forged Referer, an unauthenticated caller can hit `/embed/best?embed_url=...` and, when no embed exists, trigger `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, embed_url: embed_url)` (see `EmbedController#best`), which leads to `TopicRetriever` doing server-side fetch/import (`TopicEmbed.import_remote` via `open(url)`), only constrained to the configured `embeddable_host`. The Redis throttle in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` is per-URL key (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`), so varying paths bypasses it. This matches the finding that referer-based auth is insecure and the endpoint is effectively unauthenticated for triggering retrieval/refresh.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The postMessage origin check uses substring containment (`discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`) instead of strict equality, so any origin whose string contains the Discourse URL passes. A malicious origin such as `http://evil.com/?http://forum.example.com` or a subdomain-suffix trick containing the full discourse URL substring sends `discourse-resize` messages that the embedding page accepts; because the handler only sets iframe height the direct impact is limited (no sensitive data read), but the weak origin gate is a latent XSS/data-theft primitive if the handler ever grows to trust message payloads — and the correct fix (===, or parsed-origin comparison) is one line.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, the check is `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`, i.e., it tests whether `discourseUrl` contains `e.origin` as a substring. The finding claims the opposite (that any origin containing the Discourse URL would pass), but with the code as written a longer malicious origin like `http://evil.com/?http://forum.example.com` or `http://forum.example.com.evil.com` would *not* be contained within `discourseUrl` and would be rejected. While strict origin equality would be cleaner, the specific bypass scenarios described are not supported by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' tests verify nothing about those guards: feed_polling_enabled? is not stubbed in them, so the real SiteSetting default (feed_polling_enabled: false in config/site_settings.yml) short-circuits execute and poll_feed is never called regardless of the setting under test. Deleting the `SiteSetting.feed_polling_url.present?` or `SiteSetting.embed_by_username.present?` conditions from Jobs::PollFeed#execute would still pass this suite, so a regression that polls a nil feed URL (crashing `open(nil)` in poll_feed) ships green.

adjudication.rationale: In spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb, the "requires feed_polling_url" and "requires embed_by_username" examples only stub feed_polling_url/embed_by_username to nil and expect poll_feed to never run, but they do not stub SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?. Since site_settings.yml sets feed_polling_enabled: false by default, Jobs::PollFeed#execute (which gates on feed_polling_enabled? && feed_polling_url.present? && embed_by_username.present?) will short-circuit on the first condition and the tests will pass even if the other guards were removed. This is a real, diff-grounded issue with the tests’ effectiveness, not a demonstrated runtime bug in the production logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The 'is 404 without an embed_url' test attributes the failure to the missing embed_url, but the before_filter ensure_embeddable runs before params.require and raises Discourse::InvalidAccess first because SiteSetting.embeddable_host is '' (unstubbed in this test), so params.require(:embed_url) is never reached. Removing the `params.require(:embed_url)` guard from EmbedController#best would not fail this test; the test's assertion (`response.should_not be_success`) is satisfied by the host-check rejection it actually exercises, giving false confidence that the param contract is covered.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, `before_filter :ensure_embeddable` runs before `embed_url = params.require(:embed_url)` and raises `Discourse::InvalidAccess` if `SiteSetting.embeddable_host.blank?` (default in `config/site_settings.yml` is `''`). In `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb`, the test `it "is 404 without an embed_url"` does `get :best` without stubbing `embeddable_host` (or referer), so it will fail due to the host-check rejection rather than missing `embed_url`. Thus the finding correctly identifies that the test doesn't actually cover the `params.require(:embed_url)` contract and could pass even if that guard were removed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The 'creates a topic view' test replaces the unit under test with a mock: TopicView.expects(:new) returns nil, so @topic_view is nil, and since the spec never calls render_views, the best.html.erb template (which dereferences @topic_view.posts and @topic_view.topic.url) is never rendered — the test asserts the mock was constructed and nothing else. A regression that assigns @topic_view = nil, passes wrong options, or breaks the view template entirely still passes this test; the only success-path assertion lives in the shared `after` block which never touches rendered content or assigns.

adjudication.rationale: In spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb, the “creates a topic view when a topic_id is found” example sets `TopicView.expects(:new).with(123, nil, {best: 5})` but does not specify a return value, so `TopicView.new` will return `nil` under Mocha defaults and `@topic_view` would be `nil` in the controller action. Because the spec does not call `render_views`, the `best.html.erb` template (which dereferences `@topic_view.posts` and `@topic_view.topic.url`) is never rendered, so this test only asserts the constructor call and the generic success/header checks in the shared `after` block. This is a diff-grounded test weakness, but it’s not a verified production defect in the application code itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Every test in the 'with a valid host' context stubs retrieved_recently?, so the real throttle implementation in TopicRetriever (the $redis setnx/expire 60-second logic, including the no_throttle: true branch used by Jobs::RetrieveTopic for staff) is never executed by any test in the diff. A regression in retrieved_recently? — e.g. the setnx key never expiring, permanently blocking all embed retrievals, or the no_throttle flag being ignored so staff are throttled too — passes this suite untouched, and the production symptom is embedded comment threads that never populate.

adjudication.rationale: In spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb, within the "with a valid host" context both examples stub `retrieved_recently?` (one returns false, one returns true), so the real throttling implementation in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` (the `$redis.setnx` + `expire 60` logic and the `return false if @opts[:no_throttle]` branch) is never exercised by any test added in this diff. `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` passes `no_throttle: user.try(:staff?)`, but there is no test covering that behavior either. This is a concrete test-coverage gap for newly added nontrivial logic, not a directly verifiable functional bug in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] All five tests stub or expect perform_retrieve, so the entire retrieval pipeline the spec file nominally guards — perform_retrieve's existing-embed bail, the PollFeed trigger, and fetch_http's user lookup / import_remote call — has zero executed coverage in this diff. The path that Jobs::RetrieveTopic actually invokes in production (TopicRetriever#retrieve → perform_retrieve → fetch_http) can regress arbitrarily — e.g. fetch_http crashing on a missing embed_by_username user being nil and .downcase raising NoMethodError — without any test failing.

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb` there are five examples and each one either `expects(:perform_retrieve).never` or `expects(:perform_retrieve).once` (with `retrieved_recently?` stubbed), meaning `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` (and thus its `TopicEmbed.exists?` early return, optional `Jobs::PollFeed` call, and `fetch_http` path) is never actually executed under test in this diff. Other specs mock `TopicRetriever#retrieve` (`spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb`) or only test `Jobs::PollFeed#execute` gating, so they also don’t cover `perform_retrieve`/`fetch_http` behavior. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test coverage gap for newly added nontrivial logic, not a directly verifiable functional bug claim.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The 'Supports updating the post' test asserts only `post.cooked =~ /new contents/`, which is trivially true under raw_html cooking (cooked == raw), so it never verifies the revision machinery the update path exercises — PostRevisor#revise! with skip_validations/bypass_rate_limiter, or that embed.content_sha1 is updated to prevent re-revision. A regression where TopicEmbed#import skips the revisor entirely (returning the stale post) or never updates content_sha1 (re-revising every post on every hourly poll) still passes this test; RSS-driven sites silently churn revisions or never pick up edits.

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb`, the update test (`"Supports updating the post"`) only checks that the returned `post.cooked` matches `/new contents/` after calling `TopicEmbed.import` a second time. Given `Post#cook` returns `raw` when `cook_method == :raw_html` (added in `app/models/post.rb`), this assertion confirms the raw content changed, but it does not verify the specific update-path machinery in `TopicEmbed.import` (the `PostRevisor#revise!` call in `app/models/topic_embed.rb`) nor does it check that `embed.content_sha1` is updated via `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)`. A regression where `content_sha1` is not updated (causing repeated revisions on each poll) would not be caught by this test.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new cook short-circuit `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` skips Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...) entirely — a behavior change in the core cooking pipeline with no test anywhere in the diff that registers or asserts an after_post_cook filter against a raw_html post. A plugin relying on after_post_cook (e.g. to sanitize injected HTML on every cooked post) is silently dropped for RSS-imported posts, and since topic_embed_spec only asserts `post.cooked == post.raw`, the filter-skipping behavior is an untested divergence from the documented cook contract.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `Post#cook` to immediately `return raw` when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (app/models/post.rb), which verifiably bypasses `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)` for those posts. The new `TopicEmbed`/RSS import path explicitly sets `cook_method: ...[:raw_html]` (app/models/topic_embed.rb), and the added spec only asserts `post.cooked == post.raw` (spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb) without any coverage that an `:after_post_cook` filter still runs (or intentionally does not). This is a concrete, diff-grounded behavior change / contract concern for plugins, but the diff doesn’t prove it is definitively incorrect in core, so it’s better categorized as an important review concern rather than a guaranteed defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The success assertions (`response.should be_success`, X-Frame-Options header) live in an `after` block rather than per-example `it` assertions, so any example added inside the 'success' context that merely exercises a broken branch still 'passes' via the after block's evaluation of the last successful request state, and a failing header check is reported against whichever example ran last. Future test authors adding cases to this context get misleading failure attribution and an implicit success contract that reads as a side effect rather than an assertion, degrading change-safety of the controller spec.

adjudication.rationale: In spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb, the "success" context places `response.should be_success` and the `X-Frame-Options` header assertion inside an `after` hook rather than inside each `it` block. This is verifiable in the diff and is a test-structure issue: any future example added to that context that forgets to issue a request (or exercises a different request/branch) would still run the shared `after` expectations against whatever `response` object is present for that example, and failures would be reported as coming from the example even though the assertion isn't local to it. This degrades clarity/change-safety but isn't an application behavior defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] An already-shipped migration (CreateTopTopics, dated 20131223, i.e. present on existing production databases) was retroactively edited to add `force: true` to its create_table, making the migration destructive on re-run. On any environment that already ran this migration and then re-runs it (db:migrate:redo, a rollback/down followed by up, or restoring schema_migrations state after a partial deploy), `create_table :top_topics, force: true` silently DROPs the existing top_topics table and all its rows — computed top-topic metrics data is irreversibly destroyed with no backup step, and the drop happens inside a migration whose down cannot restore the data.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly modifies an existing migration `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb`, changing `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. In Rails, `force: true` drops the table if it already exists before creating it, which can silently destroy existing `top_topics` data on any re-run/redo/rollback+up scenario. Because this is a retroactive edit to a dated migration, it creates a real data-loss hazard that the migration’s `down` path cannot restore.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new TopicEmbeds migration uses `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`, building destructive behavior into the migration itself. If this table ever exists when the migration runs again (a re-run after a failed deploy where the transaction committed, a restore, or an operator re-running pending migrations against a partially-migrated DB), all topic_embeds rows are silently dropped; TopicEmbed.import then re-creates duplicate topics for every embedded URL because the embed_url uniqueness record is gone. A plain create_table would fail loudly instead.

adjudication.rationale: The migration `20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb` does `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`, which in Rails will drop the table if it already exists before recreating it. That is inherently destructive and would silently delete existing `topic_embeds` rows in any scenario where the migration (or an equivalent schema-load/redo) runs against a DB that already has the table. The diff also shows `TopicEmbed.import` relies on `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` to decide whether to create a new topic/post vs update, so if the table were dropped/recreated (losing the embed_url tracking), subsequent imports would indeed create duplicate topics for URLs that previously existed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `embed_url` is a 255-char varchar with a unique index, but embed URLs from real-world pages (long query strings, tracking params) routinely exceed 255 characters and there is no truncation or length validation upstream. TopicEmbed.import on a >255-char feed item link raises a value-too-long error (MySQL strict / PG) inside the PollFeed job with `retry: false`, aborting processing of all remaining feed items in that run; on MySQL non-strict it silently truncates, which then collides on the unique index with a different URL sharing the truncated prefix, failing the import with a duplicate-key error on a URL that was never embedded.

adjudication.rationale: The migration creates `topic_embeds.embed_url` as a Rails `string` (default 255 chars) with a **unique index** (`add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`), but the code paths that populate it (`TopicEmbed.import` and `TopicEmbed.import_remote`) accept arbitrary URLs and only validate via a regex (`return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`), with no length validation/truncation. `Jobs::PollFeed` parses feed items and calls `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, ...)` inside an `rss.items.each` loop, and the job is configured with `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so an exception from inserting an overlong URL would abort the run and skip remaining items. The unique-index/truncation collision scenario is also consistent with this schema/code combination on DBs that truncate silently.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] topic_id and post_id are plain integer columns with null: false but no foreign-key constraints and no composite uniqueness, while TopicEmbed rows are the sole record mapping an embed_url to its topic. If a referenced topic or post is later deleted (e.g., by a moderator purge or a deletion routine that doesn't know about topic_embeds), the topic_embeds row survives as an orphan; TopicEmbed.import then takes the update path, calls PostRevisor.new(nil-post).revise! and raises NoMethodError, permanently breaking re-import and the embed/best view for that URL until the stale row is manually cleaned up — there is no cleanup path in this diff.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `topic_embeds` with `topic_id`/`post_id` as plain integers (migration `CreateTopicEmbeds`) and no FK constraints or `dependent:` cleanup on the `belongs_to` associations. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path does `post = embed.post` and then unconditionally `PostRevisor.new(post)` when content changes. If the referenced post/topic has been deleted, `embed.post` can be `nil`, causing an exception when revising (no nil-guard or cleanup exists in this diff). This can break re-import and embed rendering for that URL until the stale row is removed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] content_sha1 is committed via update_column without checking the result of PostRevisor#revise!, so a failed revision permanently marks the content as imported. If revise! fails (returns false, or @post.save with validate: false still fails at the DB level), embed.content_sha1 is updated anyway, so every subsequent poll/feed import sees the hash as unchanged and never retries the update — the topic silently diverges from the source article forever with no error logged.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, when an existing embed is updated (`else` branch), the code calls `revisor.revise!(user, ..., skip_validations: true, bypass_rate_limiter: true)` and then unconditionally executes `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). The diff also shows `PostRevisor#revise!` can return `false` early (`return false if not should_revise?`) and, even when it proceeds, `update_post` does `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])` without checking the boolean result before continuing (lib/post_revisor.rb). Therefore, it is verifiable from the diff that a failed/ignored revision (either early false or a failed save) can still lead to `content_sha1` being updated, preventing future retries and leaving the post content out of sync with the source.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] import_remote calls open(url) with no timeout and reads the entire body into memory with no size cap. A slow or hung embeddable host blocks the Sidekiq RetrieveTopic worker (and the scheduled PollFeed path that reaches here) indefinitely on a stalled TCP connection, and a huge page OOMs the worker process; this runs on the request-triggered /embed/best path, so one bad target URL wedges the job queue's workers.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import_remote` the code does `open(url).read` (lib/open-uri semantics) with no explicit timeouts or response size limits, then passes the entire body to `Readability::Document` (`app/models/topic_embed.rb`). This can block indefinitely on a stalled connection and can allocate unbounded memory on very large responses. The call path is reachable from the request-triggered `/embed/best` flow via `EmbedController#best` enqueueing `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`, which calls `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` → `TopicEmbed.import_remote`; it’s also reachable from feed polling (`TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` calling `Jobs::PollFeed`, which itself uses `SimpleRSS.parse open(...)` without timeouts). This is a real robustness/DoS defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] poll_feed calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) with no timeout, and the job is configured sidekiq_options retry: false. A hung feed server blocks the scheduled job worker indefinitely, and any exception (network error, malformed feed, nil i.content causing NoMethodError on scrub) fails the job with retries disabled — feed importing silently stops for all subsequent hours until someone notices, with no surfaced error to any operator.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the job does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with no explicit timeouts or rescue. Because it’s a scheduled Sidekiq job with `sidekiq_options retry: false`, any network exception or parsing/processing error will fail the run without retries. Additionally, `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` can raise `NoMethodError` if `i.content` is nil. A hung `open` call can also block the worker thread indefinitely. These failure modes are directly present in the diff and can break feed importing reliability.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The retrieved_recently? throttle key is committed via $redis.setnx before perform_retrieve runs, so a failed or retried retrieval no-ops 'successfully'. When perform_retrieve raises (open-uri error, Readability parse failure), Sidekiq's default retry re-runs RetrieveTopic, but the 60-second throttle key makes the retried job silently skip the retrieval and report success — the TopicEmbed is never created and the client-side loading page reload loop never converges on content.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?`, the Redis throttle key (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`) is set via `$redis.setnx` and `expire(60)` *before* `perform_retrieve` runs, and `retrieve` skips `perform_retrieve` when `retrieved_recently?` returns true. Since `perform_retrieve` can raise (e.g., `open(url).read` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote`), a failed `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` run will still have set the throttle key; a Sidekiq retry occurring within 60s will then no-op (no exception, no retrieval) and the job will be marked successful, potentially leaving the embed uncreated until the key expires and another trigger happens.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The loading page unconditionally reloads every 30 seconds with no failure path and no retry cap. An end user on the embedding site whose retrieve job failed (invalid content, fetch error, throttle collision) gets an infinite reload loop of the 'Loading Discussion...' page for as long as they leave the page open — the failure is invisible to them and to the site operator, with no error state ever rendered.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb` which unconditionally executes `setTimeout(function() { document.location.reload(); }, 30000);` with no retry cap or error state. `EmbedController#best` renders this loading template whenever `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is nil and simply enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)`. If the job never results in a `TopicEmbed` record (e.g., fetch/import fails, `TopicRetriever` bails out, user missing), the client will remain in an infinite reload loop with no visible failure path, as the finding describes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] feed_key (the modified-hash Redis key) is computed but never read or written, so the intended poll-throttle/dedup mechanism is inert. Whoever later relies on feed-modified:* to avoid re-parsing unchanged feeds finds it absent; meanwhile every hourly run re-parses the full feed and re-runs import for every item, relying solely on content_sha1 comparison inside a transaction that can raise and abort the whole feed on one bad item.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `feed_key` is defined (computes `"feed-modified:#{Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(...)}`) but is never referenced anywhere in the diff, so any Redis-based throttle/dedup it implies is not actually implemented. The job as added will parse the feed and iterate all `rss.items` every run (`SimpleRSS.parse open(...)` then `rss.items.each`), relying on `TopicEmbed.import`'s per-item `content_sha1` check to avoid updates, which is an efficiency/robustness concern rather than a directly broken behavior. The additional claim about `feed-modified:*` being absent is consistent with the unused method, but the diff does not show any consumer that expects it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The update branch assumes embed.post is present; a nil post (post deleted, embed row left behind) crashes PostRevisor with NoMethodError. A poll cycle or user-triggered retrieve hitting an embed row whose post was deleted raises inside the Sidekiq job; with retry: false on PollFeed this takes down the entire remaining feed import for that run, and with the retriever's throttle key already committed the user's embed stays broken for 60s with no surfaced error.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path does `post = embed.post` and then unconditionally instantiates `PostRevisor.new(post)` when `content_sha1` changed (app/models/topic_embed.rb). If the associated post was deleted (leaving the `topic_embeds` row), `embed.post` will be nil and this will raise (likely NoMethodError inside PostRevisor usage). That exception would also abort the `rss.items.each` loop in `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb), and since the job has `sidekiq_options retry: false`, the rest of the feed import for that run would be skipped. Additionally, `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` sets the Redis throttle key before `perform_retrieve` runs (lib/topic_retriever.rb), so a crash in `perform_retrieve` would leave the 60s throttle in place with no handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The raw_html cook path returns raw before Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...), silently bypassing all registered post-cook plugins for these posts. Any site relying on a plugin that rewrites cooked output (e.g., onebox transformation, lazy-image rewriting) finds imported embed posts skip the filter with no warning; the next change that assumes the filter always runs gets harder to reason about because the bypass is undocumented in the plugin contract.

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/post.rb, Post#cook now has an early return for raw_html (`return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`), which bypasses the subsequent `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)` call. This is a real, diff-grounded behavioral change for posts created with `cook_method: :raw_html` (see TopicEmbed.import passing `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`). Whether this is a defect depends on intended plugin semantics, but the bypass is real and could surprise plugins expecting `:after_post_cook` to always run.
